title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. Π_{0,3} = π_1(P^1−{0,1,∞}) is free on two generators, and Π̂_{0,3} is its profinite completion. 𝔖^+_{0,3} is an extension of 𝔖_3 by Π_{0,3}. It is generated by an involution σ_∞ and an element ρ of order 3, with relations σ_∞^2 = ρ^3 = 1. So it is Z/2 * Z/3 ≅ PSL(2,Z), with Π_{0,3} ≅ Γ(2)/±1 as the kernel of PSL(2,Z) → PSL(2,F_2) ≅ 𝔖_3. Its profinite completion 𝔖̂^+_{0,3} is the profinite free product Z/2 ∐ Z/3. The page is §VI, 'Automorphisms with loop structure (à lacets) of Π̂_{0,3} and 𝔖̂^+_{0,3}'. Its purpose is to set up the 'équation des lacets' that the whole folder 'variations sur l'équation des lacets' is about.

Diagram (49) has four corners.
- Top left: Autext(𝔖̂^+)′, the outer automorphisms inducing the identity on the quotient 𝔖_3.
- Top right: Autext^𝔖(Π̂)′, the outer automorphisms of Π̂ commuting with the outer 𝔖_3-action. The top arrow is restriction and is claimed to be an isomorphism.
- Bottom left: Aut(𝔖̂^+, σ_∞)′, the automorphisms fixing σ_∞ and fixing ρ mod Π̂.
- Bottom right: Aut(Π̂, σ_∞), the automorphisms of Π̂ commuting with int(σ_∞) and commuting with int(ρ) up to inner automorphisms. The bottom arrow is restriction and is claimed to be an isomorphism.
- The vertical arrows are the obvious maps, also claimed to be isomorphisms.

The margin records the standing assumption that the centre of 𝔖̂^+_{0,3} is trivial. Under that assumption 𝔖̂^+ embeds into 𝒢 = Aut(𝔖̂^+)′, giving a chain Π ⊂ 𝔖̂^+ ⊂ 𝒢.

Parametrisation (50)–(53). An element u of Aut(𝔖̂^+, σ_∞)′ is determined by u(σ_∞) = σ_∞ and u(ρ) = gρ with g ∈ Π̂. Equivalently, in 𝒢 one has uρu^{-1}ρ^{-1} = g.
- Since ρ has order 3, g must satisfy (gρ)^3 = 1. Expanding gives gρgρgρ = g·ρ(g)·ρ^2(g)·ρ^3, where ρ(g) = ρgρ^{-1}. So the condition is the boxed loop equation (51): g ρ(g) ρ^2(g) = 1.
- Condition (53) adds that σ_∞ and gρ, subject only to σ_∞^2 = (gρ)^3 = 1, again present 𝔖̂^+. This is exactly what makes the endomorphism an automorphism.
- The result is a bijection between Aut(𝔖̂^+, σ_∞)′ and the set of g ∈ Π̂ satisfying (51) and (53).

Next page (97). Grothendieck imposes the inertia ('lacets') condition: u(ℓ_i) = int(g_i) ℓ_i^p, with a multiplier p = χ(u) ∈ Ẑ^*. He also derives g_1 = gρ(g_0) and g_∞ = gρ(g)ρ^2(g_0).

Modern reading. This is the profinite presentation of the Grothendieck–Teichmüller relations coming from PSL(2,Z) = Z/2*Z/3. Fixing σ_∞ is the 2-cycle relation (I). (gρ)^3 = 1 is the 3-cycle relation (II), here before normalising away the inertia exponents; the m-terms of Drinfeld's relation (II) appear once g is written in terms of f and the inertia exponent p = λ. The group cut out this way, inertia-preserving outer automorphisms of F̂_2 commuting with 𝔖_3, contains GT̂. It lacks only the pentagon relation, which needs M_{0,5}.
errors: No outright mathematical errors. The computation (gρ)^3 = gρ(g)ρ^2(g)ρ^3 is correct.
Gap acknowledged in the margin: the triviality of the centre of Z/2 ∐ Z/3 (profinite) is only assumed ('On admet ici').

Unacknowledged gap: the vertical isomorphisms also need two facts, the uniqueness of the σ_∞-fixing representative and conjugacy of involutions in the profinite free product. Neither is proved; both follow from later results on torsion and centralizers in profinite free products (Herfort–Ribes, mid-1980s, as I recall).
Existence argument for the vertical arrows: if u(σ_∞) = hσ_∞h^{-1}, then h mod Π̂ centralises σ̄_∞ in 𝔖_3, so h can be chosen in Π̂ after multiplying by σ_∞. This is fine but implicit on the page.

ideas.what: Identifying 𝔖-equivariant outer automorphisms of Π̂_{0,3} with automorphisms of the profinite Z/2*Z/3 fixing the involution σ_∞ (diagram 49)
ideas.modern_name: Out^{𝔖_3}(F̂_2) versus Aut(PSL(2,Ẑ)-type completion of Z/2*Z/3); the 'GT via PSL2(Z)' viewpoint
ideas.usually_credited_to: Drinfeld (1990) for GT̂; Ihara; Lochak–Schneps (1990s) for the Z/2*Z/3 interpretation
ideas.where_published: Spirit appears in Esquisse d'un programme (1984); the explicit diagram is possibly in La Longue Marche (1981, circulated/edited later), unsure

ideas.what: Loop equation g ρ(g) ρ^2(g) = 1, equivalent to (gρ)^3 = 1, parametrising these automorphisms
ideas.modern_name: 3-cycle (hexagon-type) relation (II) of the Grothendieck–Teichmüller group, before inertia normalisation
ideas.where_published: Possibly La Longue Marche à travers la théorie de Galois (1981); not in Esquisse explicitly

ideas.what: Presentation condition (53): σ_∞ and gρ must again generate 𝔖̂^+ with only the relations σ_∞^2 = (gρ)^3 = 1, so that u is bijective
ideas.modern_name: Invertibility condition on (λ,f) in GT̂ (the group-like versus monoid GT̂ issue)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Drinfeld; Ihara (GT̂ as a group versus the monoid of solutions)

ideas.what: Triviality of the centre of profinite Z/2 ∐ Z/3, assumed

missed.claim: Dated around 1981, this page derives from scratch, via the presentation PSL(2,Z) = Z/2*Z/3 (σ_∞^2 = ρ^3 = 1), the relations later known as relations (I)–(II) of Drinfeld's GT̂ (1990). Relation (II) appears here in a normalisation-free form, gρ(g)ρ^2(g) = 1, and on the next page the inertia multiplier χ(u) = λ is introduced. This is a priority/historical point: GT-type equations were written by Grothendieck about nine years before Drinfeld. It is partially known to specialists (Schneps and others have discussed the Longue Marche) but is not standardly credited.
missed.quote: g∈Π̂_{0,3} est assujetti à la condition (51) gρ(g)ρ²(g)=1 qui exprime la relation (52) (gρ)³=1
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical credit for GT̂. The unnormalised form u(ρ) = gρ, with g ranging over the whole profinite free group and the inertia condition separated out, is close to the 'GT via Out(F̂_2)^{𝔖_3}, inertia-preserving' characterisations later proved by Lochak–Schneps, Harbater–Schneps and Hoshi–Minamide–Mochizuki.

missed.claim: The page treats the group Aut(𝔖̂^+, σ_∞)′ before any inertia condition is imposed, i.e. all g satisfying (51) and (53). The structure of this larger group is not determined here. In particular, which solutions of (51) are not inertia-preserving, and how big the group is compared with GT̂, is not settled here; this looks like a natural point to check against the later literature.
missed.quote: On trouve ainsi une corr. 1-1 entre les éléments de Aut(𝔖̂⁺_{0,3},σ_∞)′ et les g∈Π̂_{0,3} satisfaisant (51)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This links to whether outer automorphisms of F̂_2 commuting with 𝔖_3 are automatically inertia-preserving (the 'unnormalised' versus GT̂ question), which is related to later results on group-theoreticity of inertia.

deep.surprise_reason: This is an explicit early (around 1981) derivation of the Grothendieck–Teichmüller 2- and 3-cycle relations from Z/2*Z/3. That is notable for priority, but it is consistent with what is known of the Longue Marche and Esquisse, and specialists such as Schneps are aware Grothendieck worked with such equations. Hence moderate, not high.
transcription_corrections: Diagram top right: 'Aut ext^𝔖(Π̂_{0,3})′', described as 'groupe des autom. extérieurs qui commutent à l'action ext. de 𝔖_3'.
Bottom-left description reads 'groupe des autom. de 𝔖̂⁺_{0,3} qui fixent σ_∞, et qui fixent ρ mod Π_{0,3}'. The struck-through word is the first 'fixent', not a word before it.
Bottom-right description reads 'groupe des a. qui commutent à σ_∞, et qui commutent extt. à ρ'.
Line (50): 'u(ρ)=gρ (i.e. uρu^{-1}ρ^{-1}=g)'. The second clause is computed in 𝒢, where u is viewed as an element of the automorphism group.
The struck word in the left margin near the diagram looks like 'Exhaustive'/'Descriptive', crossed out.
Margin chain reads approximately 'Π_{0,3} ⊂ 𝔖̂^×_{0,3} ⊂ 𝒢' and 'NB On admet ici que le centre de 𝔖̂^×_{0,3} est trivial'. The superscript looks like × or +.

Margin text reads 'On écrit les formules dans Aut(𝔖̂⁺_{0,3})′ = 𝒢, groupe des autom. de 𝔖̂⁺_{0,3} induisant l'identité sur 𝔖̂⁺_{0,3}/Π_{0,3} ≃ 𝔖_3'. The word 'extérieurs' is inserted, and 'intérieurs' may be a candidate reading.
